methodological_rigor.justification: Design is appropriate and rigorous: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational (135 sites, 25 countries) phase II/III with a prespecified 2-in-1 adaptive design, central IRT randomization, stratification by PD-L1 CPS and HPV status, and oversight by an IDMC with prespecified futility criteria (ΔORR<0% and ΔDCR<0%). Statistical methods are appropriate for time-to-event endpoints (stratified log-rank, Cox with Efron tie handling), with Miettinen–Nurminen for ORR/DCR and a stated event-driven sample size (n=374 target). Legitimate limitations are acknowledged: ctDNA/biomarker analyses are explicitly post hoc with small BEP subsets, no exposure-adjusted AE analysis was performed, and p-values are omitted because no hypothesis testing was planned at this interim. The adaptive-decision analysis population and censoring patterns (data immature, high early censoring) are described but could have benefitted from a sensitivity analysis for OS beyond the futility read-out.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with central randomization and prespecified endpoints, mapping to Oxford LoE 1b. The clinical question is important (1L R/M HNSCC where pembrolizumab ± chemotherapy is SOC) and endpoints are patient-relevant (OS, PFS, ORR, HRQoL, safety). The negative result — with HRs favoring placebo (OS HR 1.51; PFS HR 1.40) — directly informs development decisions, has already prompted termination of further feladilimab development in HNSCC, and contributes to a growing evidence base against novel checkpoint-partner combinations in this disease (CheckMate 651, KESTREL, EAGLE, KEYNOTE-669). The ctDNA-stratified exploratory signal is hypothesis-generating but not practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT applies given the randomized design. Reporting is generally thorough: trial registration (NCT04128696), eligibility criteria, protocol amendment history (May 19, 2020), stratification factors, blinding, central randomization via IRT, prespecified primary/secondary endpoints, prespecified adaptive decision criteria, IDMC role, and AE summaries including grade ≥3 AESIs and treatment-related deaths. A CONSORT-style patient flow is cited (Fig. 1), but exact randomization numbers per arm, allocation concealment mechanism details, and formal CONSORT item-by-item checklist are not visible in the text. Data/code availability is not stated in the blinded manuscript (reasonable given blinding), and sharing of individual-level trial data, PGx data, and ctDNA/NGS data is not described — hence a low data availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical: this is the definitive randomized evaluation of an ICOS agonist (feladilimab) plus pembrolizumab in 1L PD-L1+ R/M HNSCC, following a promising single-arm phase I signal in INDUCE-1. The negative finding is important for the field and challenges the ICOS target in HNSCC, but conceptually it adds to a documented pattern of failed PD-1-partner combinations (CheckMate 651, KESTREL, EAGLE, KEYNOTE-669 all cited). The ctDNA baseline-stratified exploratory analysis and integration of germline PGx (HLA heterozygosity, HLA evolutionary divergence, skin autoimmunity PRS) with ICB response offer modest methodological novelty but are underpowered and hypothesis-generating. Positioning in the literature is appropriate and does not overclaim.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, logically organized, and uses standard oncology terminology with acronyms defined (ICOS, CPS, mITT, BEP, TMB, TIS, PRS). The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded with HRs and CIs, accurately reflecting the negative primary result. The Discussion is balanced, candidly addresses the counterintuitive finding (possible Treg stimulation by feladilimab, data immaturity), and situates the result within concurrent HNSCC combination-trial failures. Minor issues: the adaptive decision criteria section contains duplicated bullet text that reads as a formatting artifact, and figure/table captions are informative but somewhat terse for standalone interpretation.

key_strengths: Rigorous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design with prespecified 2-in-1 adaptive methodology, central randomization, and IDMC-triggered futility stop
Clinically important negative result in 1L PD-L1+ R/M HNSCC that directly informs ICOS-targeting drug development and the broader anti–PD-1 combination strategy
Comprehensive endpoint reporting (OS, PFS, ORR, DCR, HRQoL, safety) with HRs and 95% CIs, plus candid acknowledgment of early censoring and data immaturity
Integrated exploratory biomarker program (ctDNA, TMB, HLA PGx, TIS, TME signatures) that generates testable hypotheses for future HNSCC immunotherapy trials
key_concerns: ctDNA and PGx subgroup analyses are explicitly post hoc with small BEP sizes (BEP1 n=145; BEP2 n=97) and limited capacity to adjust for multiplicity
No exposure-adjusted AE analysis despite the counterintuitive finding of more TRAEs in the placebo arm
Data and code availability are not described; no deposition of PGx or ctDNA data is referenced in the blinded text
Duplicated bullet text in the adaptive decision criteria section and terse figure legends slightly undermine presentation polish
Causal mechanism for the apparent detriment with feladilimab–pembrolizumab (e.g., Treg stimulation) is speculative, with no on-treatment biospecimens available to test it
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid randomized phase II/III with an important, clearly reported negative result and sensible exploratory biomarker work; fits tier 2 (JIF ~10–19) where high-quality negative RCTs with translational depth are routinely published, with minor revisions to clarify data availability and formatting.
